article.title: Rachel Reeves says UK’s future is in EU as she backs Andy Burnham on Brexit

article.content: Former chancellor says leaving European Union has made Britain ‘poorer, weaker and less secure’ The former chancellor Rachel Reeves has argued the UK’s future should be inside the EU, saying Brexit has made the UK “poorer, weaker and less secure”. Writing in the Sunday Times , the Labour former cabinet minister said she welcomed “Andy Burnham’s leadership” after remarks made by the prime minister in recent days fuelled questions about the prospect of Britain returning to the bloc or adopting its freedom of movement rules. Continue reading...
article.aiArticle:
Former chancellor **Rachel Reeves** has stated that the long-term future of the United Kingdom belongs inside the European Union, aligning herself with the position held by **Andy Burnham** on Brexit. According to a report by **World news | The Guardian**, Reeves argued that the decision to leave the political and economic bloc has left the country in a diminished state. 

Writing publicly on the matter, the former chancellor asserted that the departure from the EU has rendered Britain noticeably poorer, weaker, and less secure. Her intervention brings renewed attention to the ongoing debate over the nation's post-Brexit trajectory and its diplomatic and economic ties with European neighbors. The remarks echo broader discussions regarding fiscal strategy and governance, drawing parallels to recent debates such as those highlighted in a recent critique arguing that [this budget fails to live up to Andy Burnham’s grand rhetoric](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/this-budget-fails-to-live-up-to-andy-burnham-s-grand-rhetoric).

## The Broader Context of Brexit and Public Finance

The debate over the UK's relationship with the European Union remains one of the most polarizing topics in British politics. Since the 2016 referendum and the formal exit, successive administrations have grappled with trade barriers, regulatory alignment, and labor shortages. While proponents of Brexit argued it would restore national sovereignty and economic independence, critics continue to point to sluggish growth and trade friction as evidence of structural damage to the economy.

## Why This Matters

*Context:* For British businesses, policymakers, and citizens, the question of European integration directly impacts trade costs, regulatory frameworks, and geopolitical stability. A former chancellor advocating for a return to the EU signals deep-seated anxieties among some political figures regarding the country's long-term economic competitiveness outside the single market. This stance opens up broader discussions about whether future administrations might seek closer institutional ties, which could face skepticism from voters who prioritized leaving the bloc. Observers tracking economic policies may also find connections to related debates, including discussions on whether [Andy Burnham admits he would have liked more radical first budget](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/andy-burnham-admits-he-would-have-liked-more-radical-first-budget) changes.

## What to Watch

*Context:* Analysts will be monitoring how current and prospective political leaders respond to Reeves' remarks, particularly regarding whether opposition figures or government members adopt a more pro-European stance in upcoming policy platforms. Future public statements from both Reeves and Burnham will indicate if this signals a coordinated shift toward revisiting the UK's long-term trade and diplomatic alignment with Brussels.

Sources: [World news | The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/01/rachel-reeves-uk-future-is-in-eu-andy-burnham-brexit)
